problem: The justification that X(t)=A is SSS only shows that each single-time value has the distribution of A. Strict stationarity is a statement about every finite-dimensional joint CDF, so the given reason is incomplete and a student may think checking marginals is enough.
fix: Add: for any times t₁,…,tₙ the vector (X(t₁),…,X(tₙ)) equals (A,…,A), so its joint CDF is the distribution of A in every coordinate and does not change under a shift h.

problem: The time average is evaluated only over a whole number of cycles. That shows the average along a special subsequence of record lengths, not the limit as T→∞ for arbitrary T, so the ergodicity conclusion rests on a special case.
fix: Note that ∫₀ᵀ2cos(2πt+θ)dt=(1/π)[sin(2πT+θ)−sin θ] is bounded by 2/π for every θ, so (1/T)∫₀ᵀ2cos(2πt+θ)dt→0 V as T→∞; whole cycles are just the easy case where the integral is exactly zero.

problem: The question asks for two properties of R_X(τ) but the answer lists three (R_X(0)=E[X(t)²], evenness, and the Cauchy–Schwarz bound), which does not match the 2-mark demand.
fix: Either say 'state any two' in the question, or keep exactly two properties in the answer and move |R_X(τ)|≤R_X(0) to the exam traps.
